name: Girawa
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Pick 2020 UH diss (read) covers N. Adelbert but states stress data 'minimal or nonexistent' for most languages; no Girawa stress statement

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32) covers only Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan and says 'the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'; Girawa (Mabuso) is outside its scope and appears only in the bibliography ('Gasaway, Eileen, Patricia M. Lillie, and Heather Sims. 1992. Girawa grammar. Unpublished'; 'Lillie 1999. Girawa dictionary. Unpublished manuscript. SIL archives, Ukarumpa').

sources.citation: Lillie, Pat. [1999] (posted 2005). Girawa dictionary. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics. (Glottolog ref 64758, 47 pp.; PDF is 6 large pages; SIL entry 47685 in PDF keywords; data collected 1976-1999)
sources.note: Introduction (p.1) gives the alphabet and a letter-by-letter pronunciation guide ('k is a glottal stop', diphthongs ai/au/ei/oi/ou); nothing at all on stress, accent or syllable structure; headwords carry no stress marks (grep stress/accent = 0 hits in extracted text and scanned text).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (Girawa = column C2)
sources.note: Semi-phonemic wordlist transcription with no stress marks and no statement on stress (0 hits); p. ix notes only sound fluctuations for Girawa (s~h, z~y, zy~w~e, ?~k).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Classification only (Girawa C2, 3,568 speakers; Bagasin-Girawa belongs to the Mabuso Stock); nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: p. 6 (sec. 1.3): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Bagasin/Girawa is mentioned only in the classification discussion (Claassen wordlist vs. author's; 'a checkup in the field is called for'); no Girawa phonological data.

sources.citation: Grambank (Just & Lorenzen) Girawa page; TransNewGuinea.org Girawa page; Wikipedia 'Girawa language'; Rosetta Project Girawa Swadesh list
sources.note: Grambank cites only Gasaway & Sims 1992 (no stress features); TNG lexicon from Z'graggen 1980 only; Wikipedia is a stub; Swadesh list has no stress marks. Nothing on stress.
